Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

factor noun

something that helps bring about a result

also a factor, key factor, contributing factor, count for a lot, tip the balance

classical

Liv. 21.4.2: ut pater in sē minimum mōmentum ad favōrem conciliandum esset
Caes. BC 3.70: ita parvae rēs magnum in utramque partem mōmentum habuērunt

mōmentum, mōmentī n.

noun, second declension

a factor, something that tips the balance; weight, influence

Properly the weight that tips a balance, and so a circumstance that decides an outcome: magnum mōmentum habēre, to be a big factor. Lewis & Short: “a cause, a circumstance; weight, influence, importance”. Of time, a moment (see moment).

Examples

  • dein brevī effēcit, ut pater in sē minimum mōmentum ad favōrem conciliandum esset

    soon he made his father the least of the factors that won him favourLiv. 21.4.2

  • quod saepe in bellō parvīs mōmentīs magnī cāsūs intercēderent

    because in war great reversals often turn on small factorsCaes. BC 1.21.1

  • Minimīs mōmentīs, patrēs cōnscrīptī, maximae inclīnātiōnēs temporum fīunt

    The greatest turns of fortune, senators, come about through the smallest factorsCic. Phil. 5.26

Other words

  • valēre ad — count for something in, be a factor in

    phrase: valeō with ad and the accusative, often a gerund · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.182: valet igitur multum ad vincendum probārī mōrēs … eōrum, quī agent causās; Cic. Phil. 9.12: multum valuisse ad patris honōrem pietās fīliī vidēbitur (Lewis & Short)

    Multum valet ad, it is a big factor in; nihil valet ad, it plays no part in.

  • causa, causae f. — a cause, one of the reasons

    noun, first declension · also used · classical

    See reason and cause: in causā esse, to be a cause (Livy).

See also cause, reason, important, influence.

SourcesLewis & Short: momentum · Lewis & Short: valeo · Lewis & Short: causa
